rubric_items.reason: All 8 acceptance criteria and the 300-character fact map to REQ-1..REQ-17; extra scope is listed under Out of scope.
REQ-16 is now one checkable case (prior F-1 fixed). REQ-8 still bundles three list controls, and REQ-17 mixes a display rule with a classification statement.
Every known REQ cites its ticket line, baseline or glossary entry; REQ-17 cites A-01, which says 'Show it as is'. Nothing invented.
The free-text reason vs no-medical-history-in-lists clash was put to the user as Q-01, answered in A-01, and recorded as a mismatch citing the baseline.
One question, with real options and a proposed default, put to the user; now answered. No open questions remain.
Plain wording; glossary status terms (Cancelled, Scheduled, Completed, No-show, Medical history) used consistently.

findings.text: Prior F-2 still open: REQ-8 bundles three behaviours (status filter, date range, paging) in one requirement.

cites.quote: The column follows the list's status filter, date range and paging.

findings.suggested_fix: Split into one REQ per list control, or state one testable condition covering all three.

findings.text: Prior F-3 still open: two Out-of-scope entries give no reason for exclusion.

cites.quote: Sorting or searching the list by cancellation reason.
Changing how a reason is entered, its length limit, or which statuses have one.

findings.suggested_fix: Add a reason to each, e.g. 'not asked by HMS-33'.

findings.text: Prior F-4 still open: Known says REQ-1 to REQ-15 map to criteria 1-8 'one behaviour each', yet REQ-6 and REQ-9 are then listed as derived, so the mapping is inexact.

cites.quote: REQ-1 to REQ-15: ticket acceptance criteria 1 to 8, one behaviour each.

findings.suggested_fix: List which criterion each REQ comes from, and mark REQ-6 and REQ-9 as derived.

findings.text: REQ-17 joins a testable display rule (shown as entered, no filtering) with a classification statement (appointment data, not medical history) that a tester cannot check as list behaviour.

cites.quote: the reason is appointment data, not one of the patient's medical-history fields.

findings.suggested_fix: Keep the display rule in REQ-17 and move the classification to the A-01 mismatch or a note.

Medical history appears only on the patient's own page, never in lists
